title: Private/VPC: Pull-through Caching & Certificate Rotation Policy (PRD + Acceptance)
creator: Lena Park
description: Product requirements and acceptance criteria for a controlled pull-through caching strategy and in-place certificate rotation for Private/VPC deployments. Objective is to allow secure, auditable artifact distribution and certificate lifecycle operations while minimizing required egress windows and giving operators deterministic rollback and recovery options.
background: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs have two recurring operational pain points: (1) safely distributing large binary artifacts (images, bundles, model shards) with minimal or no sustained egress, and (2) rotating TLS certificates / signing material without forcing full cluster redeploys or extended connectivity to Redwood control plane. Existing docs focus on mirror-based staged upgrades; this PRD defines an alternate pattern centered on a pull-through caching proxy and an operator-driven cert-rotation workflow that reduces risk for long-lived air-gapped tenants.
goals: Provide a supported pull-through caching blueprint (proxy + signed cache manifest) that customers can run in an isolated subnet to seed and serve artifacts locally
Define a certificate rotation workflow that allows operator-triggered rotation with automated health checks and audit logs, without restoring egress for full cluster bootstrap
Ensure upgrade flows using the cache are reproducible and auditable; all artifacts are signature-verified before install
Minimize maximum required egress time for routine patching and emergency upgrades
Surface deterministic acceptance criteria and runbook steps for SRE and field engineering teams
non_goals: Provide a turnkey, managed artifact mirror service hosted by Redwood (customers continue to operate cache within their VPC)
Redesign of low-level package signing algorithms (we rely on existing signing/provenance mechanisms)
Solving for intermittent consumer networks inside the VPC; local operator responsibility remains
requirements: REQ-1: Pull-through cache component must support HTTPS origin and S3-compatible backends with optional proxy-auth and be deployable as a single Kubernetes deployment or OCI container image
REQ-2: Cache must expose an immutable, signed manifest of cached artifacts; manifest signatures must be verifiable using customer-provided keys or Redwood-supplied verifier tooling
REQ-3: Cache must support TTL and manual pinning of artifacts to avoid eviction during upgrades

REQ-4: Certificate rotation must support a dual-active period where both old and new certs are accepted for control-plane and agent TLS handshakes for a configurable window (default 10 minutes), with automatic fallback on health-check failure

REQ-5: Upgrade orchestration must be able to operate in two modes: online (with temporary egress to origin) and offline (using only the local cache and signed manifests), with explicit operator confirmation for offline mode
REQ-6: All upgrade/install operations must verify artifact signatures and log verification status to the local audit store and Redwood-compatible telemetry for customers that opt-in
REQ-7: Provide CLI commands and console documentation for: cache seeding, manifest signing/verification, cert-rotation dry-run, and rollback
REQ-8: Provide metrics and health endpoints for cache hit-rate, artifact verification failures, cert-expiry window, and last-successful-sync timestamp
REQ-9: Security: private keys used for signing or certificate generation must never be transmitted to Redwood; tooling should support HSM/KMS usage and offline signing workflows
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Given a freshly provisioned Private cluster with the pull-through cache deployed in the customer VPC, the operator can seed the cache from a signed artifact bundle and complete a runtime patch upgrade using only the cache (no outbound egress) within a documented playbook

AC-2: During an operator-triggered certificate rotation, agents and control-plane components successfully negotiate TLS using the dual-active window; if >50% of nodes fail health checks after rotation, automated rollback restores the previous cert within 5 minutes

AC-3: Artifact verification records are present in the local audit store for every artifact applied during an upgrade, each record includes artifact digest, signer key id, verification result, and timestamp

AC-4: Cache reports metrics with <1 second latency for health endpoints and exports a hit-rate metric; end-to-end upgrade using the cache shows >90% cache hit-rate for model and runtime artifacts in test harness

AC-5: The offline upgrade playbook documents the maximum expected egress time for the seeding operation (seed windows) and provides recovery steps if seeding is interrupted; field-run acceptance test demonstrates successful recovery from interrupted seed with operator guidance
AC-6: Security review sign-off obtained and documented; threat model updated to include the pull-through cache and cert rotation flows
AC-7: CLI tooling for dry-run cert rotation produces a simulated plan and does not change live certificates; test-run validates no disruption in a staging VPC
network_constraints: Network must allow outbound HTTPS to specified origins during explicit seed windows; otherwise cache seeding must be performed via removable media or a pre-signed bundle
Cache deployment should be colocated in a subnet with access to private registries and storage backends; operator must ensure appropriate routing/NAT for temporary seeding
Minimal required open ports: 443 for origin fetches (only during seed), 8443 for local cache API, and 10250 for node agent reachability if required by local orchestration
airgap_workflow: Option A: Signed bundle transfer — operator exports a signed artifact tarball (with manifest) from an online environment, verifies signature locally, and imports into cache via sftp or USB

Option B: Temporary controlled egress — operator opens a narrowly scoped egress window using customer firewall rules to allow the cache to pull artifacts from specified origin endpoints; window duration must be strictly documented and logged
Option C: Hybrid — initial seed via signed bundle, subsequent delta updates via short egress windows triggered by operator with manifest-driven verification
upgrade_strategy: Two-mode orchestrator: 'offline-mode' reads manifests and fetches solely from local cache; 'online-mode' can fetch missing artifacts from configured origins with explicit operator approval. Upgrade controller must support canary subsets and provide a forced-rollback hook that re-applies prior manifest if health checks fail.
runbook_high_level: 1) Validate cache health and manifest signature 2) Put cluster into maintenance mode 3) Execute dry-run upgrade in a canary namespace 4) If canary passes, roll to majority with progressive rollout 5) Monitor verification audit logs and metrics 6) Complete and exit maintenance mode or rollback on failures
test_plan: TP-1: Integration test that seeds cache via Option A (signed bundle) and completes a minor runtime upgrade in a lab VPC with no outbound egress
TP-2: Chaotic seed test where seeding is interrupted mid-transfer; validate recovery steps in the playbook
TP-3: Cert rotation dry-run and canary rotation with simulated certificate expiry and health-check failure to validate automatic rollback
TP-4: Performance test measuring cache hit-rate and artifact verification latency under concurrent upgrade load (50 parallel installs)
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if artifact verification fails for >1% of artifacts during a single upgrade operation
Alert when last-successful-sync is older than configurable threshold (default 72 hours)
SLO: cache API 99.9% uptime during maintenance windows; documented fallback to artifact-airgap-runbook if SLO breached
Audit log retention default 90 days with export path documented for on-prem archives
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Operator misconfigures origin endpoints causing unwanted egress. Mitigation: Validate origin list against an allowlist and require operator confirmation with an explicit checklist.
Risk: Stale cache leading to failed upgrades. Mitigation: Provide TTL, pinning primitives, and preflight verification that compares manifest digests to expected release manifest.
Risk: Key compromise in signing workflow. Mitigation: Support offline signing with HSM/KMS and require key-ids in manifests; rotate signer keys on a defined cadence
dependencies: ENG-21140 (cache image and helm chart delivery)
milestones: M1: Prototype cache + manifest signing tooling (2026-03-01)
M2: Field test with two customers using Option A (2026-04-01)
M4: GA release for private deployments (2026-05-01)
notes: This PRD intentionally separates the artifact distribution problem from full mirror strategies; it is targeted at customers who prefer operator-controlled seeding and minimal ongoing egress. Implementation must be flexible to support both cloud-backed origins and entirely offline signed-bundle workflows.
